findings.title: Race condition in device-limit enforcement
findings.body: CreateOrUpdateDevice first calls CountDevices and only if count < deviceLimit proceeds with the upsert. Between the count check and the insert there is no locking/transaction, so concurrent requests can all pass the check and insert simultaneously, allowing the device count to exceed deviceLimit. The limit is a soft, racy guard rather than a hard limit.

findings.title: Anonymous authentication now fails synchronously when device-tagging fails
findings.body: Previously TagDevice was invoked asynchronously in a goroutine so tagging failures (including DB errors) never blocked authentication. Now Authenticate calls TagDevice synchronously and returns the error directly (not just for ErrDeviceLimitReached but anything propagated from TagDevice/tagDeviceUI/CreateOrUpdateDevice), which will cause Authenticate to fail and reject anonymous access on any device-tagging error, e.g. transient DB issues, not just when the limit is actually reached. This changes behavior for all non-limit errors from 'warn and continue' to 'fail the request'. Also, running TagDevice synchronously now adds a DB round trip to every anonymous request's auth path, which could have a performance impact that wasn't present before (the removed goroutine had a timeout and panic recovery that are no longer present).

findings.title: TagDevice now propagates all tagDeviceUI errors, not just the device-limit error
findings.body: The change added `return err` after `a.tagDeviceUI(...)` fails, so any error returned by tagDeviceUI/CreateOrUpdateDevice (not only ErrDeviceLimitReached) is now returned to the caller (Authenticate), which will cause anonymous authentication to fail on any device creation error (e.g. transient DB failures), whereas previously such errors were only logged and ignored.
